Consult Summary:
- A physically active patient presents with new right knee pain and clicking after increased training for a marathon; symptoms began ~2 weeks ago with pain first appearing around mile 2–3, worsened with running, and improving with ice; plan includes ice therapy, running modification, physiotherapy evaluation, and consideration of a stronger anti-inflammatory and possible knee imaging if symptoms persist or worsen.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Right knee pain with clicking during and after longer runs; concern for structural injury.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms started ~2 weeks ago; pain begins after about 20 minutes of running (around mile 2.5–3); pain persists with continued running; recently some swelling initially which resolved with ice; currently not swollen.
- Exacerbating factors: Prolonged running, longer runs; clicking and pain increase during flexion/extension (gym exercises).
- Relieving factors: Ice therapy; reducing running distance/intensity (recommendation to ease up on running).
- Associated symptoms: Transient tingling in the right toes after a run.
- Other joint symptoms: No pain in other joints; no back pain; no swelling of hands/feet/elbows/wrists; no locking when sitting or stairs pain; able to fully straighten and flex the knee.
- Systems review: Denies systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss) or significant cardiovascular or respiratory symptoms.
- Relevant past medical history: Prior ice-hockey injury with a significant bruise a few months ago; prior UTI with ER visit (kidney stones suspected in ED); Lasik for farsightedness; generally healthy otherwise.
- Medications and substances: Ibuprofen (400 mg dose; route/frequency not documented); Naproxen (Aleve) – dose/route/frequency not documented; Vitamin D; Melatonin; Xanax (dose/route/frequency not documented); occasional cannabis use ("smoke a joint"); other OTC acetaminophen/NSAID use not clearly differentiated.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Social history: Active marathon training; cannabis use; no tobacco use documented; otherwise active lifestyle.
- Family history: Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Knee injury: Bruise from ice hockey several months ago.
- UTI with ER visit; suspected kidney stones (noted in narrative).
- Lasik surgery for farsightedness.
- No chronic medical illnesses described.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen — 400 mg; route/frequency not documented.
- Naproxen (Aleve) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Vitamin D — dose not documented.
- Melatonin — dose not documented.
- Xanax — dose not documented.
- Cannabis use — not a medication; noted as social history.
- All other medications/doses not documented.

- Cannabis use (smoking a joint).
- No alcohol use documented.

- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam findings: Not documented.

Investigations:
- No imaging or laboratory studies performed to date.
- Plan includes possible imaging if persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever, or locking occurs.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Right knee pain with mechanical symptoms (clicking) and activity-lue pain in the setting of marathon training; no current instability or locking; past mild swelling.
  - Plan:
    - Ice therapy: continue as much as possible.
    - Activity modification: ease running; avoid pain-inducing activities; avoid pushing through significant pain.
    - Pharmacologic: continue ibuprofen; consider prescribing a stronger anti-inflammatory for regular use in future (name not specified) but not with ibuprofen; ensure dosing with food.
    - Referral: arrange referral to physiotherapist for comprehensive knee assessment.
    - Imaging: consider knee imaging if persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever, or knee completely locks; otherwise evaluate with physiotherapist first or in-clinic if waiting times are long.
- Issue 2: Right toe tingling after runs.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor; address as part of knee/physiotherapy assessment; no standalone imaging or treatment indicated at this time.
- Issue 3: Prior knee injury and intermittent swelling (historical).
  - Plan:
    - Reassess in physiotherapy evaluation; correlate with current symptoms.
- General plan:
  - Maintain ice therapy; modify training to reduce pain and risk of further injury.
  - Referral to physiotherapist for a long assessment and knee examination.
  - If symptoms worsen or signs of infection or knee locking develop, seek urgent evaluation.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vitals; detailed physical examination findings; specific imaging results; complete medication dosing and routes for all listed meds; documented allergies.
- Internal conflicts: None identified in transcript.
- Transcript quality: Generally coherent; some details (exact doses/routes for several meds) are not documented; no audio/clarity issues noted beyond missing data.
